questions.stem: What happened at a construction site in Brooklyn on Tuesday?
options: A) A man was pulled to safety after a building collapse.
B) A beam about ten feet long collapsed to the ground.
C) A rescue worker got trapped in the basement.
D) A deserted 100-year-old building caught fire.

explain.定位:
Rescue crews pulled a man to safety after a collapse at a construction site in Brooklyn
on Tuesday.
周二，在布鲁克林一处建筑工地发生坍塌后，救援队把一名男子救出脱险。
explain.信号:
新闻开篇第一句总述。答案信号是"新闻第一句"：Rescue crews pulled a man to safety
after a collapse at a construction site in Brooklyn on Tuesday. 出现在录音最开头，新
闻惯例是首句一句话交代核心事件，What happened 的答案就在这里，无需再往后找。
explain.替换:
pulled a man to safety ↔ A man was pulled to safety
主被动转换
after a collapse at a construction site ↔ after a building collapse
概括替换
explain.排除:
B) 原词陷阱
B 盗用了录音里 trapped under a beam about 10 feet below the surface 中的 beam 和
ten feet，拼成 A beam about ten feet long collapsed to the ground.，但录音说的
是"被困在地表以下约 10 英尺处的一根横梁下"，不是"一根约 10 英尺长的横梁塌到地
上"——10 英尺指的是深度不是梁长，且塌的是楼不是梁，答非所问。
借用原文：He was trapped under a beam about 10 feet below the surface
C) 张冠李戴
C 盗用录音里 buried up to his waist in the basement 的 basement 和"被困"概念，拼成
A rescue worker got trapped in the basement.，但录音里被困在地下室的是一名"non-
worker civilian"（非工人平民），救援人员（Rescue crews）是去救人的，被困者与救援
者张冠李戴。
借用原文：A man described as a "non-worker civilian" was buried up to his waist in the basement.
D) 与原文相反
D 盗用录音结尾 It was the site of a 2006 fire 里的 fire 和 100-year-old building，拼成
A deserted 100-year-old building caught fire.，但录音说火灾是 2006 年的旧事、这栋
百年楼此后一直空置；周二发生的是坍塌不是着火，把陈年旧事当成本次主事件了。
借用原文：It was the site of a 2006 fire and has remained vacant ever since.

questions.stem: What does the report say about the "non-worker civilian"?
options: A) He suffered a fatal injury in an accident.
B) He once served in a fire department.
C) He was collecting building materials.
D) He moved into his neighbor's old house.

explain.定位:
The man was collecting building materials when the first floor collapsed underneath him.
当一楼在这名男子脚下坍塌时，他正在收集建筑材料。
explain.信号:
描述此人当时行为的直陈句。答案信号是"录音中正面交代此人行为的那一句"：The man
was collecting building materials when the first floor collapsed underneath him. 直
接说明事发当时这名平民在做什么（收集建材），正是题干问"报道关于此人说了什么"的
落点。
explain.替换:
The man was collecting building materials ↔ He was collecting building materials
近乎原句替主语
explain.排除:
A) 与原文相反
A 称 He suffered a fatal injury in an accident.（在事故中受致命伤），但录音明说 he is
in stable condition with non-life-threatening injuries（情况稳定、伤势无生命危险），
fatal（致命）与 non-life-threatening（无生命危险）正好相反，伤情程度被反向夸大。
借用原文：Officials said he is in stable condition with non-life-threatening injuries.
B) 原词陷阱
B 盗用录音里 The Fire Department of New York 中的 fire department，编成 He once
served in a fire department.（他曾在消防部门任职），但录音里 Fire Department 是发
布消息的官方机构，从未说这名平民当过消防员，是把机构名硬安成此人的过去职业。
借用原文：The Fire Department of New York says the vacant 100-year-old building being pulled
down partially collapsed.
D) 张冠李戴
D 称 He moved into his neighbor's old house.（他搬进了邻居的旧屋），盗用录音
purchased by a neighboring church 里的 neighboring（邻近的）一词，但录音说的是
这栋百年楼"被邻近的一座教堂买下"，且无人搬入（楼一直空置），主体（教堂 vs 此人）
和动作（买下 vs 搬入）都被掉包。
借用原文：The building was reportedly purchased by a neighboring church in 2011.
Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.
1 Millions of people are struggling to understand their paychecks or calculate money in shops,
campaigners have said. Being bad at maths should no longer be seen as a badge of honor or down to
genetics, according to National Numeracy, a new organization which aims to challenge the nation's
negative view of the subject. Chris Humphries, chairman of the group, said that poor maths skills can
affect an individual's life, leaving them at a higher risk of being excluded from school, or out of work.
"Figures from a government survey, published last year, show that 17 million adults in England have
basic maths skills that are, at best, the same as an 11-year-old," he said. Speaking at the launch of
National Numeracy, Mr. Humphries said, "That's a scary figure, because what it means is they often can't
calculate or give change." Mike Ellicock, chief executive of National Numeracy, said, "We want to
challenge this 'I can't do maths' attitude that is prevalent in the UK," adding that it was vital that all
primary school teachers understand key maths concepts, as young children who fail to learn the basics
will suffer later on.
活动人士表示,数百万人正在努力理解自己的工资单或在商店里计算金额。据National Numeracy这一新
成立的旨在挑战国家对该学科负面看法的组织称,数学不好不应再被视为一种荣誉标志或归咎于遗传。该组
织主席Chris Humphries表示,数学能力差会影响个人生活,使他们面临更高的被学校开除或失业的风险。
他说:"去年公布的一项政府调查数据显示,英格兰有1700万成年人的基础数学能力充其量与11岁儿童相
当。"Humphries先生在National Numeracy成立仪式上表示:"这是一个可怕的数字,因为这意味着他们往
往无法计算或找零。"National Numeracy首席执行官Mike Ellicock说:"我们想要挑战英国普遍存在的'我
不会数学'这种态度。"他补充说,所有小学教师理解关键数学概念至关重要,因为未能学习基础知识的幼儿日
后会受到影响。

questions.stem: What does the organization National Numeracy aim to do?
options: A) Improve the maths skills of high school teachers.
B) Change British people's negative view of maths.
C) Help British people understand their paychecks.
D) Launch a campaign to promote maths teaching.

explain.定位:
Being bad at maths should no longer be seen as a badge of honor or down to genetics,
according to National Numeracy, a new organization which aims to challenge the nation's
negative view of the subject.
据 National Numeracy（这家旨在挑战全国对数学这门学科负面看法的新机构）所说，数
学差不应再被当作一种荣耀的标志、也不应归咎于基因。
explain.信号:
aims to challenge 同义复现题干的 aim。录音里 which aims to challenge the nation's
negative view of the subject 用的正是题干同一个 aims to 信号词，后面紧跟的动作就是
机构宗旨；听到 aims to 这个与题干呼应的词，就该锁定这一句。
explain.替换:
aims to challenge the nation's negative view of the subject ↔
Change British people's negative view of maths
challenge 换 change、the subject 还原成 maths
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
选项 Improve the maths skills of high school teachers. 借了录音里 poor maths skills
的 maths skills 来诱选，但录音说的是普通成年人数学差，从没说要 "提高高中教师的数学
技能"，对象与动作都对不上。
借用原文：poor maths skills can affect an individual's life
C) 原词陷阱
选项 Help British people understand their paychecks. 抓的是录音开头 struggling to
understand their paychecks 的 paychecks（工资单）。但那只是用来描述 "人们数学差
到看不懂工资单" 的现象举例，不是机构的宗旨；机构宗旨是改变看法，不是专门教人看工
资单。
借用原文：struggling to understand their paychecks or calculate money in shops
D) 未提及
选项 Launch a campaign to promote maths teaching. 听上去合理，但录音通篇只说挑
战负面看法、强调小学教师懂概念，从没提 launch a campaign（发起运动）也没说
promote maths teaching（推广数学教学），属于自己脑补，方向也偏到了 "推广教学" 而
非 "改变看法"。

questions.stem: What is vital according to the chief executive of National Numeracy?
options: A) Children take maths courses at an earlier age.
B) The public sees the value of maths in their life.
C) British people know how to do elementary calculations.
D) Primary school teachers understand basic maths concepts.

explain.定位:
Mike Ellicock, chief executive of National Numeracy, said, "We want to challenge this 'I can't
do maths' attitude that is prevalent in the UK," adding that it was vital that all primary school
teachers understand key maths concepts, as young children who fail to learn the basics will
suffer later on.
National Numeracy 首席执行官 Mike Ellicock 说："我们想挑战英国普遍存在的这种'我学
不了数学'的心态"，并补充说，至关重要的是所有小学教师都要理解关键的数学概念，因为
基础没打好的孩子日后会吃亏。
explain.信号:
vital 一词原样出现，紧跟其后即答案。录音里 it was vital that all primary school
teachers understand key maths concepts 的 vital 与题干 vital 完全同词，that 引导的从
句就是 "什么至关重要" 的答案内容；听到 vital 立刻抓其后从句。
explain.替换:
all primary school teachers understand key maths concepts ↔
Primary school teachers understand basic maths concepts
key 换成 basic，主干几乎照搬
explain.排除:
A) 偷换概念
选项 Children take maths courses at an earlier age. 看似呼应录音 young children who
fail to learn the basics will suffer later on 里的 young children，但录音说的是孩子早学
不好基础日后会吃亏，从没说要让孩子 "更早去上数学课"，把因果与措辞都改了。
借用原文：young children who fail to learn the basics will suffer later on
B) 原词陷阱
选项 The public sees the value of maths in their life. 蹭的是录音 We want to
challenge this 'I can't do maths' attitude 里讲态度的内容，但那是首席执行官说 "想挑战
的心态"，回答的是 "想做什么"，不是 "什么 vital"；而且录音并没说公众 "看到了数学的价
值"。
借用原文：We want to challenge this 'I can't do maths' attitude that is prevalent in the UK
C) 与原文相反
选项 British people know how to do elementary calculations. 借了录音 they often
can't calculate or give change 的 calculate，但录音是说很多人 "算不来、找不开零钱"
的糟糕现状，恰恰是反着的；且这话出自 chairman，不是题干限定的 chief executive，也
不是他说 vital 的内容。
借用原文：they often can't calculate or give change

questions.stem: What does the report say about the Dutch king?
options: A) He owns a fleet of aircraft.
B) He is learning to be a pilot.
C) He regards his royal duties as a burden.
D) He held a part-time job for over 20 years.

explain.定位:
The Dutch king has revealed that for more than two decades, he has held down a part-time
second job alongside his royal duties. King Willem-Alexander of the Netherlands said that he
recently ended his role as a regular "guest pilot" after 21 years with the national airline's fleet
of now-outdated aircraft.
这位荷兰国王透露，二十多年来，他在履行王室职责的同时还兼着一份业余的第二职业。荷
兰国王威廉－亚历山大说，他最近结束了在国家航空公司担任“客座飞行员”的角色，这支机
队如今使用的是过时的飞机，他干了 21 年。
explain.信号:
报道开篇点题句即落点。新闻第一句往往就是主信息，本句 he has held down a part-
time second job 直接交代了核心事实，加上 for more than two decades 和 after 21
years 两处时间数字反复强调“二十多年/21 年”，这正是答案信号——数字被反复念到的地
方多半是考点。
explain.替换:
a part-time second job ↔ a part-time job
去掉second后同义
for more than two decades ↔ for over 20 years
decades换算成years
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
选项盗用了录音里的 fleet of aircraft，但原文 the national airline's fleet of now-
outdated aircraft 说机队属于国家航空公司，他只是来当客座副驾驶，并非他“拥有”一支机
群，是听到 fleet of aircraft 就想选的原词陷阱。
借用原文：the national airline's fleet of now-outdated aircraft
B) 与原文相反
选项借用了原文 pilot/retrain to fly 的影子，但 he recently ended his role as a regular
"guest pilot" after 21 years 说明他干客座飞行员已 21 年，后面 retrain to fly the bigger
Boeing 737s 只是改飞新机型的再培训，不是“在学着当飞行员”，与原文相反。
借用原文：he recently ended his role as a regular "guest pilot" after 21 years
C) 未提及
原文恰恰相反，国王把飞行称作 a "hobby" 并说 the most relaxing part of flying，是把
它当放松的爱好；选项说他视王室职责为 burden（负担），原文根本没这么说，且情感方
向与“放松、享受”相反，属无中生有。

questions.stem: Why does the king say he likes flying?
options: A) He can demonstrate his superior piloting skills.
B) He can change his focus of attention and relax.
C) He can show his difference from other royalty.
D) He can come into closer contact with his people.

explain.定位:
"You can completely change focus and concentrate on something else. That, for me, is the
most relaxing part of flying."
“你可以完全转移注意力，专注在别的事情上。对我来说，那是飞行中最让人放松的部分。”
explain.信号:
最高级the most relaxing标出真落点。国王自述里有最高级 the most relaxing part of
flying——“最……的部分”是他强调的重点所在，正是答案信号；加上 change focus 与选项
的 change focus 呼应，定位到这句即可。
explain.替换:
change focus and concentrate on something else ↔ change his focus of attention
几乎原句改写
the most relaxing part of flying ↔ relax
形容词relaxing转动词relax
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
选项里的 piloting 来自原文反复出现的 pilot/fly，但国王说喜欢飞行是为了放松换心情，从
没说是为了 demonstrate his superior piloting skills（展示高超技术），是借飞行话题词
制造的原词陷阱。
借用原文：retrain to fly the bigger Boeing 737s
C) 未提及
选项的 royalty 借自原文 king/royal duties，但他给的理由是放松、转移注意，从没说喜欢
飞行是为了 show his difference from other royalty（显出自己跟其他王室不一样），属
无中生有。
借用原文：his royal duties
D) 张冠李戴
原文确实提到他在机场不被认出、很少人注意他，但那是讲乘客反应（第 7 题），不是他喜
欢飞行的原因；选项 come into closer contact with his people 把别处的信息安到“喜欢飞
行的原因”上，且原文 rarely recognised by passengers 反而说他没怎么和人接触，张冠李
戴。
借用原文：rarely recognised by passengers

questions.stem: What does the king say about passengers at the airport?
options: B) They liked him in his uniform.
D) They were surprised to see him.

explain.定位:
Willem-Alexander said he is rarely recognised by passengers. Very few people pay attention
to him as he walks through the airport in his airline uniform and cap.
威廉－亚历山大说，乘客很少认出他。当他穿着航空公司的制服、戴着帽子走过机场时，几
乎没什么人注意他。
explain.信号:
新闻结尾句+程度词rarely/few。这是报道末尾收束句，集中描述乘客反应，正对题干的
passengers；句中 rarely recognised 与 Very few people pay attention 两处程度词（很
少/几乎没人）是答案信号——程度词标出的正是这句的核心信息。
explain.替换:
he is rarely recognised by passengers ↔ They rarely recognised him.
被动改主动、原义不变
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
原文只说乘客很少注意他、认不出他，从没说乘客 enjoyed his company（喜欢和他相
处）；这与“几乎没人注意他”反而方向相反，属凭想象添加的反应，未提及。
B) 原词陷阱
选项里的 uniform 直接盗自原文 in his airline uniform and cap，但原文提制服是为了说
明“穿着制服走过也没人注意”，根本没说乘客 liked him in his uniform（喜欢他穿制服的样
子），是听到 uniform 就想选的原词陷阱。
借用原文：in his airline uniform and cap
D) 与原文相反
原文是乘客 rarely recognised 他、几乎没人注意他，谈不上 surprised to see him（见到
他很惊讶）——既然认不出，自然也不会因认出而惊讶，选项把反应改成了相反方向。
借用原文：he is rarely recognised by passengers

questions.stem: Why did Semenov's grandparents start a furniture plant in Bucharest?
options: A) They were skilled carpenters themselves.
B) It didn't need much capital to start with.
C) Wood supply was plentiful in Romania.
D) They saw a business opportunity there.

explain.定位:
There was a great need for furniture and my grandparents saw a business opportunity.
当时对家具有巨大的需求，我的祖父母看到了一个商机。
explain.信号:
saw a business opportunity 点出动机。被问者直接应答里出现 my grandparents saw
a business opportunity，"saw…opportunity(看到商机)"正是讲创办动机的信号词，这句
即答案句。
explain.替换:
my grandparents saw a business opportunity ↔ They saw a business opportunity there.
近乎原句、仅换主语为代词
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
They were skilled carpenters themselves. 说祖父母自己是熟练木匠，录音通篇只讲"看到
对家具的需求"，从未说他们本人会木工，属未提及的编造。
B) 原词陷阱
It didn't need much capital to start with. 里的 capital 确在录音出现——但原文 My
grandfather and father did not have much capital 讲的是"后来缺资金限制了增长"，是
公司成长的挑战，不是"创办的原因"，盗用 capital 来骗听到原词就选的人。
借用原文：did not have much capital
C) 原词陷阱
Wood supply was plentiful in Romania. 里 Romania 录音确实反复念到，但原文 A
hundred percent of our raw material comes from Romania. 是讲"原料来自罗马尼亚"，
并未说"木材供应充足"，更不是创办原因，靠地名 Romania 制造熟悉感骗人。
借用原文：comes from Romania

questions.stem: What was Semenov's grandfather trying to do?
options: A) Provide quality furniture at affordable prices.
B) Attract foreign investment to expand business.
C) Enlarge their company by hiring more workers.
D) Open some more branch companies in Germany.

explain.定位:
Their aim was to provide quality yet affordable wooden furniture.
他们的目标是提供既优质又实惠的木制家具。
explain.信号:
aim was to 直陈目标。Their aim was to provide quality yet affordable wooden
furniture 中的 aim was to(目标是)是表意图的强信号词，其后内容即"想做什么"，这句就
是答案句。
explain.替换:
provide quality yet affordable wooden furniture ↔
Provide quality furniture at affordable prices.
形容词改写成介词短语
explain.排除:
B) 原词陷阱
Attract foreign investment to expand business. 的 investment 录音念过——但 There
was also more financial investment 是"2007 年入欧后投资变多"的客观结果，不是祖
父"想做的事"，盗 investment 误导。
借用原文：more financial investment
C) 原词陷阱
Enlarge their company by hiring more workers. 暗合原文 we went from having 20
employees to 200，但那是"入欧后规模扩大"的结果，并非祖父早年的目标，把后来的扩
张说成祖父的初衷。
借用原文：from having 20 employees to 200
D) 原词陷阱
Open some more branch companies in Germany. 借 Germany 制造熟悉感——录音
our biggest market is Germany 只说德国是最大市场，从没说要在德国开分公司，纯属嫁
接。
借用原文：our biggest market is Germany

questions.stem: What does Semenov say about her company's raw materials?
options: A) They are from her hometown.
B) They are imported from Germany.
C) They all come from Romania.
D) They come from all over the continent.

explain.定位:
A hundred percent of our raw material comes from Romania.
我们百分之百的原材料都来自罗马尼亚。
explain.信号:
被问者用 Correct 应答 + 直陈来源。提问 And all the wood is local? 后，被问者答 A
hundred percent of our raw material comes from Romania.，这是对"原料来源"问句的
直接应答，comes from(来自)点明来源，即答案句。
explain.替换:
A hundred percent of our raw material comes from Romania ↔ They all come from Romania.
A hundred percent = all
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
They are from her hometown. 说原料来自"她的家乡"，录音只说来自 Romania(国家)，
从未提"家乡"，属编造。
B) 与原文相反
They are imported from Germany. 借后文 our biggest market is Germany 的
Germany 当诱饵，但德国是"销售市场"不是"原料来源"，且原文明说原料 100% 来自罗马
尼亚，与"进口自德国"正好相反。
借用原文：comes from Romania
D) 偷换概念
They come from all over the continent. 的 continent 来自 sell our products all across
the continent——但那讲的是"产品卖到全大陆"，不是"原料来自全大陆"，把销售范围偷换
成原料来源，且与"100% 来自罗马尼亚"矛盾。

在"2007 年加入欧盟"之后，all across 是范围信号，这句即答案句。

作是去试新餐厅，这句就是承载邀约的答案句。

questions.stem: What does the man say about (614) Magazine?
options: A) It is sponsored by local restaurants.

questions.stem: What does the man usually do with Susan during_____
options: A) They design a special set of menus for themselves.

spring, at a number of different price points. Susan and I go to at least three different places

所有时尚餐厅都参加。它们在那一周推出特别套餐，通常在春天，价位各不相同。我和
Susan在活动期间至少会去三家不同的餐厅。

习惯句 go to at least three…。男士说 Susan and I go to at least three different

and I，对应题干 with Susan，这句即答案句。

Susan and I go to at least three different places ↔ They go to eat at different stylish restaurants
概括加同义还原

special set menus 是原文真词，但出自 They have special set menus for the week，主

questions.stem: Why does the man say the woman is in luck?

questions.stem: What is the best way to get children to eat vegetables according to a recent study?
options: A) Rewarding them for eating vegetables.
B) Exposing them to vegetables repeatedly.
C) Improving the taste of vegetable dishes for them.
D) Explaining the benefits of eating vegetables to them.

explain.定位:
The study found that the best way to get children to eat food they do not like is simply to give
them repeated exposure to it.
这项研究发现，让孩子吃他们不喜欢的食物，最好的办法就是让他们反复接触这种食物。
explain.信号:
结论信号 the best way…is。录音里 The study found that the best way…is simply to
give them repeated exposure to it 用了「研究发现……最好的办法是……」这种明摆着下
结论的句式，结论句就是答案句，听到 the best way is 就该锁定。
explain.替换:
repeated exposure to it ↔ Exposing them to vegetables repeatedly
名词短语换成动名词、it 还原成 vegetables
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音开头确实念到家长 offer rewards or treats 给奖励，A 的 Rewarding them 就盗用了
这个原词；但紧接着说不被夸奖反而更可能去吃，奖励法是被否定的做法，不是「最好的办
法」，听到 reward 就选 A 正中陷阱。
借用原文：Some of them offer rewards or treats for children finishing their share.
C) 未提及

篇只让孩子反复尝、给奖励或夸奖，从没说过去改良蔬菜的味道，属于凭常识脑补、原文没
提。
D) 未提及
D 的 Explaining the benefits of eating vegetables（讲吃蔬菜的好处）是另一个常识里的
办法，但录音只比较了反复尝、给玩具、口头表扬三种做法，从没提向孩子讲营养好处，原
文无据。

questions.stem: What did the researchers find about carrots?
options: A) They were disliked most by children.
B) They were considered most nutritious.
C) They were least used in Belgian cooking.
D) They were essential to children's health.

口味测试显示，胡萝卜是孩子们当中最不受欢迎的蔬菜。

youngsters 出现最高级 the least-liked，正对应「四项都是最……」的选项；最高级处常是

carrots were the least-liked vegetable among youngsters ↔ They were disliked most by children

它的营养高低，B 是借最高级句式凭空生造的判断。
C) 原词陷阱
C 说胡萝卜 least used in Belgian cooking 在比利时菜里最少用，Belgian 确是录音念到的
原词（研究者来自 Belgium），听到地名就想选很危险；但录音说比利时是为了交代研究地
点，从没说胡萝卜在比利时菜里用得少，属答非所问。
借用原文：Psychologists from Ghent University in Belgium studied 98 children.

carrots 只下了「最不受欢迎」这一个结论，从没谈它对健康是否必需，纯属常识脑补。

questions.stem: What does the result of this research show?
options: A) Vegetables differ in their nutritional value.
B) Children's eating habits can be changed.
C) Parents watch closely what children eat.
D) Children's choices of food vary greatly.

explain.定位:
After the trial, 81% of children who simply tried the carrots consistently liked them. This is in
contrast to 68% for the group given a toy and 75% for the group given verbal praise.
试验结束后，单纯反复尝试胡萝卜的孩子里有 81% 一直都喜欢上了胡萝卜；相比之下，得
到玩具的那组是 68%，得到口头表扬的那组是 75%。
explain.信号:
结尾数据对比收束全段结论。录音结尾 81% of children who simply tried the carrots
consistently liked them 与 68% … and 75% 形成数据对比，篇章独白常在结尾用数据收
束主旨——这组「反复尝试组比例最高」的对比，正是整段要证明的结论落点。

81% of children who simply tried the carrots consistently liked them ↔
Children's eating habits can be changed
「原本最讨厌→反复尝后喜欢上」概括为「饮食习惯可被改变」
explain.排除:

菜，却只比较孩子喜不喜欢，从没比较它们的营养高低，A 与研究结论无关。
C) 原词陷阱
C 说 Parents watch closely what children eat 家长密切关注孩子吃什么，parents 是录音
开头真念过的原词，但开头只说家长「难让孩子吃菜、会给奖励」，从没说家长「密切关
注」，更不是这项研究的结果，属答非所问。
借用原文：All parents know it is difficult to get children to eat their vegetables.
D) 答非所问
D 说 Children's choices of food vary greatly 孩子的食物选择差异很大，录音确实测了孩
子对不同蔬菜的喜好，但研究的落点是「反复尝试能改变孩子去吃」，不是强调孩子间选择
差异大，D 答非所问、以偏概全。
借用原文：The taste tests revealed that carrots were the least-liked vegetable among youngsters.

questions.stem: What does the passage say may be unknown to many people?

questions.stem: Why has a lot of equipment been left on the moon?
options: A) It is costly to bring back.

explain.定位:

把不需要的设备运回来本会耗费燃料等宝贵资源。

项 It is damaged by radiation. 就把 radiation 搬来；但原文那句是说"研究者可研究材料
如何经受辐射"，并非说"设备被辐射损坏所以留下"，与本题问的"为何留下"风马牛不相及。

Researchers can study 直接应答题干。答案信号就是主语词 Researchers can study the

Study the effect of radiation and vacuum on its materials.

但原文从未说研究者要去"记录太空探索的细节"，研究者要做的是研究垃圾材料，record

questions.stem: What does the passage say about email?
options: A) It is likely to remain a means of business communication.
B) It is likely to be a competitor of various messaging apps.
C) It will gradually be replaced by social media.
D) It will have to be governed by specific rules.

explain.定位:
Though social media and messaging apps have taken over some of the roles from email as a
form of communication, email is likely to retain an important role for business
communication in the future.
尽管社交媒体和即时通讯软件已经接过了邮件作为沟通方式的一部分作用，邮件在未来仍很
可能在商务沟通中保留重要地位。

questions.passage:
How a Poor, Abandoned Parisian Boy Became a Top Chef

A) The busy streets in Paris were uneven and caked in thick mud, but there was always a breathtaking sight to see in the shop windows of Patisserie de la Rue de la Paix. By 1814, people crowded outside the bakery, straining for a glimpse of the latest sweet food created by the young chef who worked inside.

B) His name was Marie-Antoine Carême, and he had appeared, one day, almost out of nowhere. But in his short lifetime, which ended exactly 184 years ago today, he would forever revolutionize French gourmet food(美食), write best-selling cook books and think up magical dishes for royals and other important people.

C) Carême's childhood was one part tragedy, equal part mystery. Born the 16th child to poor parents in Paris in either 1783 or 1784, a young Carême was suddenly abandoned at the height of the French Revolution. At 8 years old, he worked as a kitchen boy for a restaurant in Paris in exchange for room and board. By age 15, he had become an apprentice(学徒) to Sylvain Bailly, a well-known dessert chef with a successful bakery in one of Paris's most fashionable neighborhoods.

D) Carême was quick at learning in the kitchen. Bailly encouraged his young apprentice to learn to read and write. Carême would often spend his free afternoons at the nearby National Library reading books on art and architecture. In the back room of the little bakery, his interest in design and his baking talent combined to work wonders—he shaped delicious masterpieces out of flour, butter and sugar.

E) In his teenage years, Carême fashioned eatable copies of the late 18th century's most famous buildings—cookies in the shape of ruins of ancient Athens and pies in the shape of ancient Chinese palaces and temples. Sylvain Bailly, his master, displayed these luxuriant creations—often as large as 4 feet tall—in his bakery windows.

F) Carême's creations soon captured the discriminating eye of a French diplomat, Charles Maurice de Talleyrand-Périgord. Around 1804, Talleyrand challenged Carême to produce a full menu for his personal castle, instructing the young baker to use local, seasonal fruits and vegetables and to avoid repeating main dishes over the course of an entire year. The experiment was a grand success and Talleyrand's association with French nobility would prove a profitable connection for Carême.

G) French Emperor Napoleon Bonaparte was known to be unimpressed by the declining taste of early 18th century cooking, but under pressure to entertain Paris's high society, he too called Carême to his kitchen at Tuileries Palace. In 1810, Carême designed the extraordinary cake for the wedding of Napoleon and his second bride, Marie-Louise of Austria. He became one of the first modern chefs to focus on the appearance of his table, not just the flavor of his dishes. "I want order and taste. A well-displayed meal is enhanced one hundred percent in my eyes," he later wrote in one of his cook books.

H) In 1816, Carême began a culinary(烹饪的) journey which would forever mark his place as history's first top chef. He voyaged to England to cook in the modern Great Kitchen of the prince regent(摄政王), George Ⅳ, and crossed continents to prepare grand banquets for the tables of Tsar Alexander Ⅰ of Russia. Never afraid to talk up his own accomplishments, a boastful Carême made a fortune as wealthy families with social ambitions invited him to their kitchens. Later, in his cook books, he would often include a sketch of himself, so that people on the street would be able to recognize—and admire—him.

I) Carême's cooking displays became the symbol of fine French dining; they were plentiful, beautiful and imposing. Guests would fall silent in wonder as servants carried Carême's fancy creations into the dining hall. For a banquet celebrating the Grand Duke Nicholas of Russia's visit to George Ⅳ's Brighton Pavilion on Jan. 18, 1817, the menu featured 120 different dishes, highlighting eight different soups, 40 main courses, and 32 desserts.

J) As he traveled through the homes of early 19th century nobility, Carême forged the new art of French gourmet food. Locked in hot kitchens, Carême created his four "mother sauces." These sauces—béchamel, velouté, espagnole and allemande—formed the central building blocks for many French main courses. He also perfected the soufflé—a baked egg dish, and introduced the standard chef's uniform—the same double-breasted white coat and tall white hat still worn by many chefs today. The white clothing conveyed an image of cleanliness, according to Carême—and in his realm, appearance was everything.

K) Between meals, Carême wrote cook books that would be used in European kitchens for the next century. His manuals including The Royal Parisian Baker and the massive five-volume Art of French Cooking Series (1833-1847, completed after his death) first systematized many basic principles of cooking, complete with drawings and step-by-step directions. Long before television cooking shows, Carême walked readers through common kitchen tasks, instructing them to "try this for yourself, at home" as famous American Chef Julia Child might do, many years later.

L) In the end, however, it was the kitchen that did Carême in. Decades of working over coal fires in tight, closed spaces with little fresh air (to ensure his dishes would not get cold) had fatally damaged his lungs. On Jan. 12, 1833, Carême died just before he turned 50.

M) But in his lifetime, Carême, ever confident, could see beyond his short domination in the kitchen. He wanted to "set the standard for beauty in classical and modern cooking, and prove to the distant future that the French chefs of the 19th century were the most famous in the world," as he wrote in his papers.

N) Decades later, chef Auguste Escoffier would build upon Carême's concept of French cuisine(烹饪). But in the very beginning, there was just Carême, the top chef who elevated dining into art.

Roughly the size of a soda can, sitting on a bookshelf, a relatively harmless gadget may be turning friends away from your home. questions.stem: In what way can the home security camera benefit visitors to your home?
options: A) It can satisfy their curiosity.
B) It can prove their innocence.
C) It can help them learn new technology.
D) It can make their visit more enjoyable.
questions.passage:
Roughly the size of a soda can, sitting on a bookshelf, a relatively harmless gadget may be turning friends away from your home. The elephant in your living room is your Internet-connected security camera, a device people are increasingly using for peace of mind in their homes. But few stop to think about the effect these devices may have on house guests. Should you tell your friends, for instance, that they're being recorded while you all watch the big game together?

"It's certainly new territory, especially as home security cameras become easier to install," says Lizzie Post, president of the Emily Post Institute, America's foremost manners advisors. "I think it will be very interesting to see what etiquette(礼仪) emerges in terms of whether you tell people you have a camera or not, and whether guests have a right to ask that it be turned off, if it's not a security issue."

Post wants to make clear that she's not talking about legal rights, but rather personal preferences. She also wants to explain that there are no right or wrong answers regarding manners on this front yet, because the technology is just now becoming mainstream. Besides, the Emily Post Institute doesn't dictate manners.

When it comes to security cameras, Post says it's a host's responsibility to make sure guests feel comfortable within their home. "I'm always a fan of being open and honest." For instance, if the host casually acknowledges that there is a camera in the room by telling a story about it, that may be enough to provide an opening for a guest to say if they are uncomfortable.

However, if a contractor is working in your home, you don't need to tell them that there are cameras watching. Then again, the air of accountability that the camera generates can also work in contractors' favor. questions.stem: Why is PepsiCo making a policy change?
options: A) To win support from the federal government.
B) To be more competitive in the global market.
C) To satisfy the growing needs for healthy foods.
D) To invest more wisely in the soft drink industry.
questions.passage:
PepsiCo is to spend billions of dollars to develop drinks and snacks and reformulate existing ones with lower sugar, salt and fat, as consumers demand healthier options and regulatory pressure intensifies amid an obesity epidemic(流行病).

The maker of Mountain Dew and Gatorade has been one of the earlier movers in the industry to offer products with reduced levels of unhealthy ingredients—PepsiCo claims a packet of its chips now contains less salt than a slice of white bread. However, its new 10-year plan makes clear it believes it still has a long way to go.

Shifting eating habits, including a sharp drop in consumption of sparkling drinks, have forced radical change on the industry. But those shifts have yet to be reflected in record obesity levels, which stand at 36.5% overall in the US.

Indra Nooyi, PepsiCo chairman, said the plan to make its products healthier was important for the company's growth. But on the subject of obesity, she pointed out that consumers' lifestyles have changed significantly, with many people being more sedentary(久坐不动的) not least because more time is spent in front of computers. She said PepsiCo's contribution was to produce healthier snacks that still tasted good.

"Society has to change its habits," she added. "We can't do much to alter sedentary lifestyles, but we can provide consumers with great-tasting products, low in salt, sugar and fat. In the past we had to have a taste trade-off. But we're breaking that trade-off."

PepsiCo's plan for its foods and drinks is based on guidelines from the World Health Organisation, which last week backed using taxes on sparkling drinks to reduce sugar consumption. Initiatives also include efforts to reduce its environmental impact, water consumption and materials used in packaging by 2025.

PepsiCo did not say exactly how much it planned to invest to reach its goals. However, Dr Mehmood Khan, chief scientific officer, said the company had doubled research and development spending in the past five years and was "committed to sustaining investment", adding that companies cannot cost-cut their way to increasing sales. PepsiCo's research and development budget in 2015 was $754 million.

translation.source: 越来越多的中国人现在的确离不开手机了。他们中的许多人，包括老年人，都使用手机应用程序(apps)保持联系并拓宽朋友圈。他们也用手机购物、查找信息，因为手机便于携带。此外，使用手机应用程序通信比传统电话便宜。然而，这种新趋势导致人们在社交时过度依赖手机。事实上，一些年轻人已经变得十分上瘾，以至于忽视了与家人和朋友面对面的交流。
translation.reference: More and more Chinese people indeed cannot live without their cell phones nowadays. Many of them, including the elderly, use mobile apps to keep in touch and expand their circle of friends. They also use cell phones to shop and search for information, because cell phones are easy to carry. Besides, communicating through mobile apps is cheaper than traditional phone calls. However, this new trend leads to people's excessive reliance on cell phones in social interactions. In fact, some young people have become so addicted that they neglect face-to-face communication with their family and friends.
